---
title: "Normal-form games"
toc: true
---

## What it is
A normal-form game describes **simultaneous** choice: players pick actions without observing others’ choices.

A (finite) two-player game is often written as payoff matrices $(A,B)$.

## What’s special
- Strategy is a complete plan: choose an action (or a mixed strategy).
- Key solution concept: **Nash equilibrium** (possibly in mixed strategies).
- Many applications reduce to identifying best responses and intersections.

## One example (matching pennies)
Player 1 chooses $H$ or $T$; player 2 chooses $H$ or $T$.

Payoffs to player 1:

$$
A=
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & -1\\
-1 & 1
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

There is **no** pure-strategy Nash equilibrium.  
In the mixed equilibrium, both players randomize:
$$
x=(1/2,1/2),\quad y=(1/2,1/2).
$$
Each player makes the other indifferent.
